question: In which Five-Year Plan was the family planning programme undertaken?
solution:
The correct answer is the __**4th Five-Year Plan**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The family planning program was undertaken in India during the Fourth Five-Year Plan, which was implemented from 1969 to 1974.
 
• The plan gave family planning the highest priority, second only to agricultural production. 
 
• The plan set targets for sterilization and IUCD insertions. 
 
• The plan aimed to reduce the birth rate from 39 per thousand population to 32 per thousand population by 1973-74. 
 
• The plan aimed to increase the number of users of conventional contraceptives from 3.24 million in 1969-70 to 10 million in 1973-74. 
 
• The plan created the Department of Family Planning within the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare. 
 
• The plan received the public commitment of the top leadership in the country. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• 2nd Five-Year Plan
 
• This plan was from 1956 to 1961 and was focused on rapid industrialization, especially in basic and heavy industries.
 
• It was also known as the Mahalanobis Plan and was based on the P.C. Mahalanobis Model. 
 
• 5th Five-Year Plan
 
• This plan was from 1974 to 1978 and was focused on removing poverty and achieving self-reliance.
 
• It introduced the Indian National Highway System for the first time. 
 
• 7th Five-Year Plan
 
• This plan was from 1985 to 1990 and had a growth rate of 6%. It was successful despite severe drought conditions for the first three years.
 
• The guiding principles of this plan were growth, equity, social justice, self-reliance, and improved efficiency and productivity.
